Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, similar sub‑problems. Each recursive call works on a reduced version of the original input and continues until it reaches a **base case**, a simple condition that stops further calls. By combining the results of these smaller calls, the original problem is solved without needing explicit loops. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: each doll (call) contains a smaller one until you finally reach the smallest doll that can’t be opened any further.
